name: Durham Community Fridges – St. Joseph's Episcopal Church
description: Outdoor community fridge and pantry run by Durham Community Fridges, a volunteer mutual-aid project ("solidarity, not charity"). Take what you need, leave what you can. This was the group's first fridge, opened in 2022.
access: No ID, no questions asked, no limits
notes: Fridge addresses come from the group's Instagram bio (checked Nov 2026). WUNC (May 2025) also lists this site. The same church hosts a free 24/7 naloxone vending machine. Fresh Start Durham's shower trailer also came here on Wednesday mornings as of Feb 2025.

name: Durham Community Fridges – Scrap Exchange (Lakewood)
description: Outdoor community fridge and pantry shelf at The Scrap Exchange in Lakewood, run by the volunteers of Durham Community Fridges. Free fresh food for anyone.
access: No ID, no questions asked
notes: Durham Food Not Bombs also shares food outside the Scrap Exchange on the first Saturday of each month.

name: Durham Community Fridges – Braggtown
description: Outdoor community fridge and pantry at Braggtown Baptist Church in north Durham, run by Durham Community Fridges. Take what you need, leave what you can.
access: No ID, no questions asked
notes: Listed in the group's Instagram bio and in its Linktree (linktr.ee/durmco), which has a fridge check-in form for this site.

name: Durham Food Not Bombs
description: All-volunteer chapter of the international Food Not Bombs movement. Shares free vegan and vegetarian meals and supplies. "Solidarity, not charity."
address: Outside The Scrap Exchange, 2050 Chapel Hill Rd., Durham, NC 27707
hours: First Saturday of each month (plus pop-ups at events around town)
access: Open to anyone, no ID or questions
notes: Its Linktree said "All planned food/supply distros are ON" (checked Nov 2026). The start time isn't posted; check Instagram @durhamfnb. Email durhamfnb@proton.me.

name: Durham Really Really Free Market
description: Monthly open-air free market where everything is free: no buying, selling, trading or bartering. Bring what you don't need and take what you do. Skills and services such as haircuts and music are welcome too.
address: Orchard Park, 1000 S. Duke St., Durham, NC
hours: 3rd Saturday of each month, 12–2 pm
access: Open to all; you don't have to bring anything to take something
notes: The Instagram bio (checked Nov 2026) listed Sat. Oct 17, 2026, 12–2 pm at Orchard Park. Check @durham.rrfm for weather cancellations.

name: Feed Durham
description: Grassroots mutual-aid collective that started during COVID. It runs free cookouts, produce and grocery giveaways (including a large Thanksgiving giveaway), neighborhood food-growing projects, and community repair clinics. Food also reaches people through dozens of partner groups.
hours: Events vary; announced on Instagram/Facebook @feeddurhamnc
access: Free, no eligibility screening
notes: Source is Civil Eats, March 2025. There is no fixed distribution site or schedule, so follow @feeddurhamnc for upcoming giveaways and repair clinics.

name: Changed Paths Durham
description: East Durham mutual-aid project. It cooks and hands out about 100 free hot meals a week, along with clothing, produce and harm reduction supplies.
access: Free, no ID
notes: Active Nov 2026 (it was running a winter supply drive). An undated community food list puts the hot meal on Sundays at 4:30 pm at Long Meadow Park, but parts of that park are closing for renovation. Confirm the current spot on Instagram @changedpathsdurham.

name: Triangle Mask Bloc
description: Volunteer mutual-aid group that gives out free masks and COVID-19 tests across Raleigh, Durham and Chapel Hill. Individuals, families and organizations can request them through an online form.
hours: Request online anytime
access: Online request form; no eligibility requirements stated
notes: Linked from Durham Community Fridges' active Linktree (Nov 2026).

name: Fresh Start Durham – Mobile Showers
description: Free mobile shower trailer with private stalls for people experiencing homelessness. Also hands out clean socks, underwear, shirts and towels, and a barber is often on site.
address: Behind Trinity United Methodist Church, 215 N. Church St., Durham, NC 27701 (Tuesdays)
hours: Tuesdays, about 7:30–11 am at Trinity UMC; Wednesdays 7–10 am at St. Joseph's Episcopal, 1902 W. Main St. (per Feb 2025 report)
access: Sign-up sheet on site. It often fills before 8:30 am on Tuesdays, so come early.
notes: Open Table Ministry's Nov 2026 calendar confirms the Tuesday showers alongside its Free Store. The Wednesday St. Joseph's site is from Feb 2025 and is unconfirmed for 2026.

name: Open Table Ministry – Free Store
description: Weekly free store for unhoused and low-income neighbors: clothing, shoes, coats, thermals, backpacks, sleeping bags and toiletries, plus coffee and Fresh Start Durham showers. It also offers case management, and county street-medicine pop-up clinics have been held at the Free Store.
hours: Tuesdays 9:30–10:30 am
access: Walk-in; no religious participation or ID requirement stated
notes: Free Store dates were listed weekly through Dec 29, 2026. It operates out of Trinity UMC but is a separate 501(c)(3).

name: Urban Ministries of Durham – Community Café, Pantry & Clothing Closet
description: Durham's main anchor for free meals: the Community Café serves 3 free meals a day, every day of the year. Also runs a food pantry and clothing closet for low-resource households and shelter residents.
hours: Café: 3 meals daily, 365 days/year (call for pantry and closet hours)
access: Serves all "regardless of race, ethnicity, religious beliefs or non-faith"
notes: Anchor listing. Specific meal times aren't posted on its site, and third-party lists disagree, so call to confirm. Lincoln CHC's Health Care for the Homeless clinic is next door at 412 Liberty St.

name: Durham Bike Co-op
description: All-volunteer community bike shop. Fix your own bike with shop tools and recycled parts, get help from volunteer mechanics, or fix up a donated bike to keep ("Need Repair or Need Bike" Sunday sessions). Also runs mobile repair clinics.
hours: DIY walk-ins Thursdays 6:30–8:30 pm (no sign-up); Need Repair/Need Bike Sundays 3–5 pm (waitlist); other DIY nights vary; see calendar
access: Membership required: $30/year OR 3 volunteer hours
notes: The calendar (durhambikecoop.corsizio.com) is active through Jan 2027. For Sunday sessions, join the waitlist; claim-a-spot links go out Fridays at 1 pm.

name: GoDurham – Fare-Free Buses
description: All GoDurham city bus routes are fare-free. You don't need a pass, ID or payment to ride.
hours: Route schedules vary
access: No fare, no ID
notes: GoDurham news headline: "GoDurham is fare-free through June 2027!" The city budget (May 2026) kept fares free, but long-term funding is uncertain.

name: Splat Space (Hackerspace)
description: Member-run nonprofit hackerspace with tools, machines, a woodshop and electronics space for hobby or freelance projects. A free public open house runs every Saturday, and free workshops are held from time to time.
hours: Public open house Saturdays 1–4 pm; members 24/7
access: Open house free to the public; kids welcome with an adult
notes: Membership is $25/mo (associate), $35/mo (student) or $60/mo (full, 24/7 key). The door is hard to find, so see splatspace.org/location.

name: Durham County Library – Innovation Lab (Makerspace)
description: Public makerspace at the Main Library with a 3D printer, Cricut/vinyl cutter, laser cutter, poster printer and craft supplies. STEAM tech and tool kits can be checked out for home or group projects.
address: Main Library, 300 N. Roxboro St., Durham, NC 27701
hours: Tue 1–5 pm, Thu 10 am–2 pm, Fri 1–5 pm, Sat 11 am–1 pm & 3–5 pm
access: Drop-in during lab hours; some equipment has material fees
notes: Hours change, so call ahead. Per-item pricing is on each equipment page. Kit checkout likely needs a library card.

name: Digging Durham Seed Library
description: Free seed-borrowing library from Durham County Library. Take up to 4 seed packets per season, and return saved seeds from your harvest if you can.
address: Main Library, 300 N. Roxboro St., Durham, NC 27701 (also East, North, South, Southwest Regional, Bragtown and Stanford L. Warren branches)
hours: Library hours; seeds usually stocked mid-February through October
access: No library card needed
notes: First come, first served while supplies last.

name: Durham County Library – Free Computers, Wi-Fi & Hotspot Lending
description: Public computers with internet and free password-free Wi-Fi at every Durham County Library branch. Printing is a small fee. Cardholders can borrow a mobile hotspot with unlimited data for 14 days. There is also monthly drop-in tech help.
address: Main Library, 300 N. Roxboro St., Durham, NC 27701 (all branches)
hours: Library hours
access: Wi-Fi open to all. Hotspots need a library card (free for county residents; photo ID plus proof of address required).
notes: The card policy doesn't address people without a permanent address, so ask staff. Hotspot rules: durhamcountylibrary.org/services/hotspot-checkout/.

name: Keep Durham Beautiful – Tool Lending Library
description: Free loans of landscaping, cleanup and beautification tools for community service projects, such as neighborhood cleanups and community gardens.
hours: Mon–Fri by appointment
access: For Durham-based community groups and organizations; request at least one week ahead
notes: Not for personal home projects. Return tools within a week of the project. Email info@keepdurhambeautiful.org.

name: Durham County Public Health – Safe Syringe Program
description: Confidential syringe services: sterile syringes, cookers, cottons, tourniquets, hygiene supplies, sharps disposal, naloxone kits, and fentanyl and xylazine test strips. Also offers HIV and hepatitis testing and referrals.
address: Human Services Building, 414 E. Main St., 1st floor, Lobby 3 (Pharmacy), Durham, NC 27701
hours: Tue & Thu 9 am–12 pm; Wed & Fri 1–4 pm
access: Confidential; ID requirement not stated
notes: For mobile SSP, text (919) 998-8152. The county notes the pharmacy closes at 12:30 pm on Fridays from Sept 18, 2026 to Jan 1, 2027, which may cancel the Friday afternoon SSP window. Call first.

name: Free Naloxone Vending Machines (Durham County)
description: Free nasal naloxone (Narcan) from vending machines. Anyone can use them, no questions asked.
address: 24/7 machines: Durham County Detention Center lobby, 219 S. Mangum St.; St. Joseph's Episcopal Church, 1902 W. Main St.; Morse Clinic, 4119 Capitol St. Weekday machine: Human Services Building lobby, 414 E. Main St.
hours: 24/7 at three sites; 414 E. Main St. Mon–Fri 8 am–5 pm
access: Anyone, no ID

name: NC Harm Reduction Coalition – Durham Syringe Services
description: Peer-based harm reduction: syringe exchange, naloxone and safer-use supplies, with deliveries, mobile outreach and a weekly fixed site. Nonjudgmental, and serves people regardless of immigration status.
address: Recovery Community of Durham office, Elizabeth St. UMC, 1209 N. Elizabeth St., Durham, NC 27701 (Fridays)
hours: Deliveries Mon 1–6 pm; mobile outreach Wed 1–6 pm; fixed site Fri 3–6 pm
access: Call, text or Signal to set up a delivery or find the mobile location. At the fixed site, knock at the Elizabeth St. door by the back lot.
notes: Contact: Loftin Wilson, loftin@nchrc.org. NCHRC was active on Durham's opioid task force in Nov 2025.

name: Durham Recovery Response Center (Crisis Receiving Center)
description: 24/7 walk-in mental health and substance use crisis center, run by RI International. Offers behavioral health urgent care, crisis stabilization, 23-hour observation, peer support and care coordination.
access: Walk-ins welcome, no appointment
notes: The site says there is no charge to guests. Its outpatient MOUD program closed in June 2025, but crisis services continue.

name: Durham HEART – 911 Crisis Response
description: City of Durham's alternative crisis response. Unarmed community response teams handle non-violent mental health, behavioral health and quality-of-life calls, including calls involving unsheltered people. Clinicians in the 911 center and follow-up care navigation are part of the program. Higher-risk calls get a clinician plus a CIT-trained officer.
access: Call 911. You can ask for a HEART response, but dispatch decides.
notes: Covers the City of Durham. HEART is not always unarmed: the co-response unit includes police. Current hours aren't posted.

name: Lincoln Community Health Center – Health Care for the Homeless Clinic
description: Primary care clinic for people experiencing homelessness, on the Urban Ministries of Durham campus. Run by Lincoln CHC, a federally qualified health center.
hours: Mon–Fri 1–5 pm; walk-ins 12:30–1 pm
access: Walk-ins accepted; care regardless of insurance or ability to pay

name: Lincoln Community Health Center – Main Site
description: Federally qualified health center offering primary care, WIC and other services. Sees everyone regardless of income, insurance status or ability to pay, with a sliding fee scale. Has several satellite clinics around Durham.
hours: Mon–Thu 8 am–8 pm; Fri 8 am–5 pm; Sat 8 am–12 pm
access: Uninsured welcome
notes: For appointments, call (919) 956-4034. Other sites include Lakewood, Holton (401 N. Driver St.), Lyon Park and Walltown.

name: Samaritan Health Center
description: Free, charitable medical and vision clinic for uninsured and underserved people, regardless of ability to pay. Lab work is included.
hours: Mon 12–5 pm; Tue 10 am–8 pm; Wed 9 am–5 pm; Thu 9 am–2 pm & 5:30–8:30 pm; Fri 9 am–1 pm
access: Apply to become a patient; no religious participation required (clinicians offer prayer only if you ask)
notes: Faith-based. Eligibility isn't on the site; an older report said uninsured Durham County residents under 200% of the poverty line, reviewed yearly. Call to confirm.

name: El Futuro
description: Bilingual (Spanish/English) outpatient mental health and substance use clinic for Latino families. Offers therapy, psychiatry, case management, support groups, parent education and peer support.
address: 2020 Chapel Hill Rd., Suite 23, Durham, NC 27707
access: Spanish-speaking clinicians
notes: The site doesn't state fees or a sliding scale, so call. It posted news regularly through Oct 2026.

name: LGBTQ Center of Durham
description: Community center with drop-in hours, drop-in case management, the Joifull Bellies food pantry, the Queer Giving Closet (free clothing), name-change navigation help, a youth drop-in and support groups.
hours: Drop-in public hours most weekdays, typically 11:30 am–1:30 pm, plus some evenings; see the calendar
access: Drop in anytime during open hours, no appointment needed
notes: The Nov 2026 calendar lists name-change drop-in and case management hours. Food pantry distributions were listed through mid-2026; check the full calendar for current pantry dates. Older lists show 1007 Broad St., which looks outdated.

name: Durham Crisis Response Center
description: Free, confidential help for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking and human trafficking. Provides a 24-hour crisis line, emergency shelter, legal advocacy, support groups and counseling referrals.
address: Durham Family Justice Center, 101 E. Morgan St., Durham, NC 27701
hours: Help line 24/7; office Mon–Fri 8:30 am–5 pm
access: Confidential
notes: Third-party directories list a Spanish-language line, (919) 519-3735, but it isn't on the DCRC homepage.

name: DEAR – Durham Expunction & Restoration Program
description: Free legal help to expunge (clear) criminal records, get certificates of relief, and restore suspended NC driver's licenses for Durham residents. Funded by the City of Durham and run from Legal Aid NC's Durham office.
address: 411 W. Chapel Hill St., Suite 1A, Durham, NC 27701
hours: Apply during the first full week of each month (online or by phone). Expungement workshop and in-person intake on the 4th Tuesday, 5:30–7 pm, at Orange Grove Missionary Baptist Church.
access: Durham residents who can't afford a private attorney
notes: The program's site runs on a Squarespace placeholder domain. Older city pages list a walk-in office at the courthouse that may be outdated.

name: Legal Aid NC – Durham Eviction Diversion Clinic
description: Free legal help for low-income Durham renters facing eviction, run with the City of Durham. Walk-in clinic at the courthouse.
address: Durham County Courthouse, 510 S. Dillard St., 3rd floor, Room 3200, Durham, NC 27701
hours: Mon–Fri 9 am–12 pm
access: Walk in or call; bring your court papers, lease and rent ledger
notes: Legal Aid NC's general helpline is 1-866-219-5262. The courthouse street address comes from a City of Durham announcement. The Legal Aid page gives only the room number.

name: El Centro Hispano – Durham
description: Latino-led community organization offering legal information and referrals, community assistance, and education and workforce programs.
address: 2000 Chapel Hill Rd., Suite 26A, Durham, NC 27707
access: Spanish spoken
notes: The site doesn't list program hours or fees, so call. A Lincoln CHC WIC clinic is in the same shopping center.

name: World Relief Durham – Immigration Legal Services
description: DOJ-recognized immigration legal services for low-income immigrants in Durham and Wake counties. Handles citizenship, DACA/TPS, family petitions, green cards and victim-based cases.
hours: By appointment
access: Consultation required before starting a case; English and Spanish
notes: The directory lists a $50 consultation fee (money order or card), so this is low-cost rather than free. Faith-based, but no religious participation is required for services. A job posting from July 2026 suggests the office is active.

name: Siembra NC – ICE Activity Hotline & Rapid Response
description: Grassroots immigrant organizing group. Its hotline takes reports of ICE or Border Patrol activity, verifies them, and sends alerts by text and social media. Also provides rapid response and safety support.
access: Anyone can call; Spanish spoken
notes: The number comes from a Durham church's Nov 2025 resource post and a Duke rapid-response page. The siembranc.org hotline page returned 404, so confirm the number on Siembra's channels.

name: Triangle Tenant Union (NC Tenants Union)
description: Grassroots tenant union that helps renters organize building-level unions to fight unsafe conditions, broken elevators, pests and retaliation. In 2025 it won Durham's tenant-defense ordinance (rent refunds when units are unlivable).
access: Open to tenants; join online
notes: Two new Durham building unions launched in March 2026. Dues info isn't published. Contact through nctenantsunion.org or Instagram @nctenantsunion.

name: Durham Beyond Policing
description: Grassroots coalition working on community safety without policing. Runs popular-education workshops (#FreeOurFam), an East Durham community design process, and campaigns to expand the HEART crisis response. Mainly organizing, not direct services.
access: Open membership
notes: Active July 2026 (East Durham community design kickoff). Contact via the form on its site or Instagram @DurhamBeyondPolicing.

name: Community Empowerment Fund – Durham
description: Relationship-based financial support and advocacy for people facing poverty and homelessness. Offers one-on-one support with savings, budgeting and housing goals, a resource database, and free community classes such as fraud prevention.
address: 2634 Durham-Chapel Hill Blvd., Suite 6, Durham, NC 27707
access: Universally accessible
notes: The Durham office hours are posted only as a flyer image, so call. A Durham Community Class was scheduled for Nov 18, 2026. A third-party list mentions a CEF community fridge inside the Durham office, but I couldn't confirm it.

name: Diaper Bank of North Carolina
description: Gives out diapers, period supplies and adult incontinence products through partner agencies. Durham partners include Urban Ministries of Durham, Family Connects and Healthy Families Durham, Durham Early Head Start and Duke Outpatient Clinic.
access: Not given directly to families; get supplies through a partner agency (some offer walk-in emergency diapers)
notes: The partner list comes from the logos on its distribution-network page, so call the bank or a partner to confirm. Email info@ncdiaperbank.org.

name: Durham Literacy Center
description: Adult literacy and GED/high school equivalency tutoring, adult ESOL (English) classes, college and career readiness, and a youth HSE program for ages 16–24.
access: Adults; youth program for ages 16–24
notes: The homepage doesn't state fees or hours, so check the enrollment page or call. It posted a newsletter in Oct 2026.

name: Book Harvest – Free Books & Family Space
description: Free children's books to build home libraries. The Family Space has free books to take home, reading nooks, toys and free storytimes (kids keep the book). Also runs outdoor Book Hubs and Book Boxes around Durham.
hours: Family Space: Tue–Sat 9am–5pm (office Mon–Fri 9am–5pm)
access: Free and open to families; children must be with an adult 16+. If the Family Space is full, books are set out front to browse and take.
notes: Book Babies: free literacy coaching and 100+ books by kindergarten for families of Medicaid-eligible newborns (enroll at bookharvest.org/book-babies). Book Hub map: bookharvest.org/find-a-book-hub. Phone is (252) 497-BOOK.
